<STRUCT_0001>
Thus we define the corresponding standard coverings of affines as follows.

Compare Schemes, Definition <REF_0001>.
Let <MATH_0001> be an affine scheme. A <TEXTITOPEN_0001>standard Zariski covering<TEXTITCLOSE_0001>
of <MATH_0002> is a Zariski covering <MATH_0003>
with each <MATH_0004> inducing an isomorphism with a standard affine open
of <MATH_0005>.

A <TEXTITOPEN_0001>big Zariski site<TEXTITCLOSE_0001> is any site <MATH_0001> as in
Sites, Definition <REF_0001> constructed as follows:
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002> Choose any set of schemes <MATH_0002>, and any set of Zariski coverings
<MATH_0003> among these schemes.
<STRUCT_0003> As underlying category of <MATH_0004>
take any category <MATH_0005> constructed as in
Sets, Lemma <REF_0002> starting with the set <MATH_0006>.
<STRUCT_0004> As coverings of <MATH_0007> choose any set of coverings as in
Sets, Lemma <REF_0003> starting with the
category <MATH_0008> and the class of Zariski coverings,
and the set <MATH_0009> chosen above.
<STRUCT_0005>

<STRUCT_0001>
It is shown in Sites, Lemma <REF_0001>
that, after having chosen the category <MATH_0001>, the
category of sheaves on <MATH_0002> does not depend on the
choice of coverings chosen in (3) above. In other words, the topos
<MATH_0003> only depends on the choice of
the category <MATH_0004>. It is shown in
Sets, Lemma <REF_0002> that these categories
are closed under many constructions of algebraic geometry, e.g.,
fibre products and taking open and closed subschemes. We can also show
that the exact choice of <MATH_0005> does not matter
too much, see Section <REF_0003>.

<STRUCT_0002><STRUCT_0003>
Another approach would be to assume the existence of a
strongly inaccessible cardinal and to define <MATH_0006>
to be the category of schemes contained in a chosen universe with
set of coverings the Zariski coverings contained in that same
universe.

<STRUCT_0004><STRUCT_0005>
Before we continue with the introduction of the big Zariski site of
a scheme <MATH_0007>, let us point out that the topology on a big Zariski site
<MATH_0008> is in some sense induced from the Zariski topology
on the category of all schemes.
